plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve pay-as-you-go account, no platform fee; GPU quota may need a request.

caveats: No universal list rate: GPU, CPU/RAM share, bandwidth and storage are host-offer-specific. Per-second compute; storage continues while stopped. Serverless uses underlying marketplace workers with no extra surcharge. Reserved prepayment up to 50% off is not a fixed tariff. Dated public API snapshots added for 1 GPU, verified hosts, reliability>=0.98; first two cheapest offers by total listed hourly price. dph_base is compute, dph_total adds default 10GB storage; bandwidth remains extra. gpu_frac describes host share, NOT fractional physical GPU.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

2026-09-28 fix pass: snapshot regimes collapsed to one per GPU (cheapest live verified offer, flag stock). Disk priced at $0.2667/GB-month = median host storage_cost across 71 live verified 1-GPU offers (range $0.08-$1.00/GB-month; the host you rent sets it; storage keeps billing while stopped). Egress $0.0052/GB = median host inet_up_cost across the same offers (host-specific; download also billed per host). Live prices moved since the earlier snapshot (e.g. H100 SXM $1.87 -> $3.09/h, H200 $3.55 -> $4.80/h).

fleet.verification: Verify email and prepay credits before renting.
fleet.notes: New accounts have a spend-rate limit, especially low before email verification; it grows over time. Docs suggest cheaper instance or waiting hours, then support chat if needed. No numeric default instance/GPU cap or guaranteed quota-raise time published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Stop Button (square icon): Pauses instance, preserves data, continues storage charges
snapshot_auto.note: Stopping keeps the container disk on the host (persistent_disk), processes/memory are not saved; no automatic checkpoint on stop/idle is documented. No idle auto-stop.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Takes a snapshot of a running container instance and pushes snapshot to the specified repository in container registry.
snapshot_on_demand.note: vastai take snapshot INSTANCE_ID --repo ... (POST /instances/take_snapshot/{id}/): docker-commit style, filesystem only (optionally pauses processes during commit), pushed to YOUR registry (docker.io default); new instances can boot from that image. Found in the official CLI source, not in the docs site (the docs page for take-snapshot 404s). Also volume clone (vastai clone volume) and vastai copy for data.

harness_api.quote: A **skill** or **plugin** lets an agent operate your **account** — find, rent, launch, and tear down instances.
harness_api.note: Vast's agent integration is the reverse direction (skills/plugins for Claude Code/Codex/Cursor that drive the Vast CLI). Inside instances only SSH/Jupyter and a constrained 'vastai execute' command API; no API to drive an agent harness in the instance.

egress_allowlist.quote: Vast.ai docker instances have full internet access, but generally do not have unique IP addresses.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side egress controls documented; Security FAQ: 'Network restrictions depend on the host configuration. Some options: Use SSH key authentication (no passwords); Configure firewall rules in your container; Select providers with static IPs for IP whitelisting'. Marketplace of third-party hosts.

egress_http_rules.quote: Network restrictions depend on the host configuration.
egress_http_rules.note: No egress controls of any kind; no HTTP-level rules.

ingress_rules.quote: You can open custom ports for any docker image using -p arguments in the docker create/run options box in the image config editor pop-up menu.
ingress_rules.note: Only control is choosing which ports are exposed (mapped to random external ports on a shared host IP, max 64). No provider-side IP allowlists or security groups (Security FAQ points to in-container firewall). Instance Portal tokens (OPEN_BUTTON_TOKEN) and Cloudflare quick tunnels are implemented inside Vast base images, not enforced by the platform.

secret_proxy.quote: Create a new user environment variable
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are account-level environment variables injected into instances (and template env); no credential-injecting proxy. Security FAQ advises 'Don't store credentials in instances'.

volume_attach.quote: We currently provide **local volumes only**, meaning: A volume is physically tied to the machine it was created on. It can only be attached to instances running on the same physical machine.
volume_attach.note: Local volumes survive instance destruction and can be reattached to new instances on the same host; fixed size; Docker instances only (not VMs); billed per GB while they exist at host-set rates. The official CLI also has 'vastai create network volume' / 'search network volumes' (network volume offers) not described in the docs guides; migration guide says 'Vast has no cross-host network volume.'

isolation.quote: Vast.ai instances run as Linux Docker containers.
isolation.note: card already models the marketplace's Docker container instance product; separate opt-in VM mode (qemu/kvm) exists but is not the modeled product

image_oci.quote: Can I use my own Docker images? Yes! ... Use standard Docker Hub, GHCR, or other registries

docker_inside.quote: Why can't I run Docker inside my instance? Docker-in-Docker is disabled for security.
docker_inside.note: the separate full-VM mode does support nested containerization, but that is not the modeled container-instance product

nested_virt.quote: Clients are isolated in unprivileged Docker containers
nested_virt.note: derived: unprivileged Docker instances have no /dev/kvm; only the separate full-VM mode advertises nested containerization, not KVM-in-KVM

desktop.quote: Browser Access (Recommended): Click the 'Open' button ... Choose between two browser-based viewers: Selkies WebRTC ... NoVNC ... VNC Client: Connect using any VNC client, Address: instance_ip:5900
desktop.note: available via the Ubuntu Desktop (VM) template

browser.note: pre-installed in the Ubuntu Desktop (VM) template

computer_use.quote: Instances are Docker containers that give you exclusive GPU access for training, inference, and development. Pay by the second, connect via SSH or Jupyter.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no screenshot/click desktop-driving API found in docs

anti_bot.quote: Instances are Docker containers that give you exclusive GPU access for training, inference, and development.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

captcha_solving.quote: Instances are Docker containers that give you exclusive GPU access for training, inference, and development.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

egress_ip_type.quote: Tier 4 datacenters have extensive physical and operational security. Individual hosts may have less formal security measures.
egress_ip_type.note: marketplace mixes vetted 'Secure Cloud' datacenter hosts and individual/community hosts (residential-type connections); no single guaranteed egress IP class

ssh.quote: Learn how to securely connect to Vast.ai instances using SSH.

snapshot.quote: Stop Button (square icon): Pauses instance, preserves data, continues storage charges
snapshot.note: disk/filesystem is preserved automatically across stop/start; GPU and running processes are not kept alive (not a memory snapshot)

fork.quote: We currently provide local volumes only, meaning: A volume is physically tied to the machine it was created on.
fork.note: only a volume-clone CLI command exists (vastai clone volume); no whole-machine clone/fork feature found

fork_running.quote: A volume is physically tied to the machine it was created on.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Stop Button (square icon): Pauses instance, preserves data, continues storage charges

pause_resume.quote: Stop Button (square icon): Pauses instance, preserves data, continues storage charges
pause_resume.note: compute/GPU billing stops while stopped; storage billing continues

wake_on_request.quote: Inactive: Stopped but data preserved (can restart if GPU available)
wake_on_request.note: stopped instances must be manually restarted; no auto-wake-on-request mechanism found

volume_shared.quote: A volume is physically tied to the machine it was created on. It can only be attached to instances running on the same physical machine.
volume_shared.note: local, single-machine volumes; no documented simultaneous multi-instance shared mount

auto_stop_idle.quote: Destroy instances you no longer need to avoid being charged for idle resources.
auto_stop_idle.note: no automatic idle-stop feature found; users are told to manually stop/destroy idle instances

live_resize.quote: Each instance has a disk storage allocation reserved at creation time. This allocation is static and cannot be changed after creation
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are also fixed proportional shares of the host tied to the GPU allocation, not independently resizable live

agent_harnesses.quote: Claude Code requires Node.js: curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | bash - ; apt-get install -y nodejs ; npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
agent_harnesses.note: coding agents are documented as something you self-install on an instance, not a preinstalled template/offering

own_agent_api.quote: A skill or plugin lets an agent operate your account — find, rent, launch, and tear down instances.
own_agent_api.note: the skills/CLI let a THIRD-PARTY coding agent control your Vast account; Vast does not offer its own browser/computer-use/research task agent

mcp_server.quote: DR-Tulu was trained end-to-end with an MCP server providing web search and page reading capabilities.
mcp_server.note: the only MCP server mentioned is a user-deployed example app running inside an instance; Vast does not ship its own first-party MCP server to control its sandboxes

lang_python.quote: Use Vast base images (also on DockerHub), which are pre-cached on many hosts
lang_python.note: default/recommended templates (PyTorch, ComfyUI, vLLM, etc.) are Python-based and ship Python out of the box

lang_node.quote: Claude Code requires Node.js: curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | bash - ; apt-get install -y nodejs
lang_node.note: Node.js is not part of the standard ML base images and must be installed manually

public_ipv4.quote: Vast.ai docker instances have full internet access, but generally do not have unique IP addresses. ... each docker instance gets a fraction of a public IP address based on a subset of ports.

inbound_https.quote: a secure Cloudflare tunnel will be created for each of your instance's open ports ... formatted like this: https://four-randomly-selected-words.trycloudflare.com

guest_firewall.quote: Can I restrict network access to my instances? ... Configure firewall rules in your container

static_egress_ip.quote: Select providers with static IPs for IP whitelisting
static_egress_ip.note: host-dependent filterable attribute (static_ip), not guaranteed for every machine

windows.quote: Instances are Docker containers that give you exclusive GPU access for training, inference, and development.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; guest OS is Linux, the 'Windows SSH Guide' is only about the client OS used to connect

macos.quote: Instances are Docker containers that give you exclusive GPU access for training, inference, and development.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

arm64.quote:
# arm64 cpu architecture only
vastai search offers 'cpu_arch=arm64'

self_host.quote: The core vocabulary of the Vast.ai platform, marketplace, offers, instances, templates, endpoints, workers.
self_host.note: not offered: Vast is a hosted marketplace connecting renters to third-party hosts, not software you self-host

byoc.quote: The core vocabulary of the Vast.ai platform, marketplace, offers, instances, templates, endpoints, workers.
byoc.note: not offered: Vast runs on marketplace hosts' own hardware, not deployed into a customer's cloud account

open_source.quote: Use Vast base images (also on DockerHub), which are pre-cached on many hosts
open_source.note: the vastai CLI and base images are open source, but the core marketplace/scheduling platform is not; not self-hostable

sso.quote: How do I secure my account? ... Use a strong, unique password ... Regularly rotate API keys
sso.note: no SAML/OIDC single sign-on documented; account security relies on password/2FA/API keys

eu_data_residency.quote: geolocation | string | two letter country code; supports =, !=, in, notin
eu_data_residency.note: renters can filter/select hosts by country (including EU countries) via the geolocation offer filter

max_session_h.quote: On-Demand (High Priority): Fixed price set by the host, Runs as long as you want, Cannot be interrupted
max_session_h.note: interruptible (spot) instances can be stopped by higher bids at any time, but on-demand/reserved instances have no fixed max duration

soc2.quote: Vast.ai has completed SOC 2 Type 2 certification. This audit, conducted by an independent third party, verified that our security, availability, and confidentiality controls meet AICPA Trust Services Criteria over a sustained observation period.

hipaa.quote: Vast.ai supports HIPAA-covered workloads on our Secure Cloud tier. Technical safeguards — including data isolation, access controls, and audit logging — align with HIPAA requirements. Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) are available for qualifying customers.
